calls.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit / identity-preserve. This is ONE anatomical key frame for a high-quality animation study, not a redesigned deer. Edit the supplied approved illustration. Preserve its exact canvas, camera, scale, face, amber eyes, muzzle, ears, spotted coat, chest/body proportions, antler tine topology and warm golden lighting. Preserve the moss/flower/stone island and three planted hoof contacts. Change ONLY the farther foreleg (the leftmost foreleg in this image), giving it a modest, anatomically correct raised step. Redraw the limb naturally: normal forearm and rounded carpal flexion, a straight rigid cannon bone folded gently backward, separate natural fetlock articulation, one correctly proportioned cloven hoof tucked slightly beneath the chest. The lifted hoof must not be thrust far forward or become an elongated hooked foot. The other foreleg and both hindlegs remain exactly planted in their existing places. All four legs must be clearly accounted for. Show believable mass and muscle continuity at the upper leg and correct occlusion against the chest, no bend in the middle of the cannon, no dislocated or rubbery joints. Keep the complete antlers and hooves inside frame. Match the approved realistic painterly detail and clean alpha. Preserve transparent exterior and soft antler glow. No background scene, no text, no UI, no pose labels, no butterfly. Output a single full-resolution frame, same 2:3 portrait composition. This is a newly drawn anatomical pose, not a geometric deformation of the photograph.

Asset: a REGISTERED 8-frame animation study atlas, 4 columns by 2 rows, all cells exactly equal, on genuine transparent background. Wide 4:3 sheet. Each cell is a full 2:3 portrait camera view of the SAME approved magical deer on the SAME moss island. No borders, numbers, labels or captions. Input 1 is the approved identity and camera/rest pose. Input 2 shows the anatomically corrected tucked foreleg shape and is the maximum flexion reference, NOT the pose for this early segment. Preserve face, eye colour, muzzle, all antler tines, coat spots, torso proportions, lighting, island, scale and position in EVERY cell. No camera movement. Frames are read left-to-right top row then bottom row. Draw EIGHT genuinely sequential closely spaced distinct poses for the FIRST QUARTER of ONE gentle curious foreleg lift-and-replace. Frame 0: exact original rest. Frame 1: subtle weight transfer, forefoot still planted. Frame 2: farther/leftmost forefoot unloads. Frame 3: heel lifts a little, hoof just releasing. Frame 4: hoof rises a few centimeters. Frame 5: small additional carpal flexion. Frame 6: hoof begins tucking gently BACK under the chest. Frame 7: forefoot is at about ONE-THIRD of the maximum lift shown by input2. The cannon must remain a straight rigid bone, with natural separate rounded carpal and fetlock articulation and normal hoof proportions. Never bend the cannon mid-shaft, form a stretched diagonal hook, or make a leg disappear. The nearer foreleg and BOTH hind legs keep exactly the same three planted hoof anchors throughout. All four limbs must be accounted for. Upper body and island are almost stationary; do not bounce or slide the entire deer. Preserve physical fur volume and correct overlap as each limb pose is REDRAWN. Generate actual anatomical pose artwork, never a squeezed/warped copy. Strict consistency of composition, margins, antlers and image identity. Detailed realistic painterly rendering identical to the reference. Large native resolution, clean alpha, full antlers/hooves inside every cell. This is sheet A, frames 0–7 of a planned 32-frame motion; do not complete the entire action on this sheet.

Asset: registered photoreal animation atlas, exactly FOUR columns by TWO rows = EIGHT equal 2:3 portrait cells; wide 4:3 canvas; genuine alpha background, no text/grid lines. These are EIGHT consecutive in-between drawings, not eight copies. Input1 is approved character identity/rest/ground. Input2 is the immediately preceding animation frame. EVERY cell must keep exactly the same full-body framing, original face/eyes/antler branching/spotted coat/body proportions and original moss island. No camera or subject-scale changes, no anatomy warping. Continue naturally from input2: all three other hooves stay planted, and the farther (image-left) foreleg makes a SMALL further tuck and starts to descend. Frame 1 matches input2's raised leg. Frame 2: carpus bends a little further, hoof stays naturally under the chest. Frame 3: maximum modest tuck, straight cannon bone, relaxed downward cloven hoof, no long hooked or broken foot. Frame 4: begin unfolding. Frame 5: hoof moves downward slightly. Frame 6: continue lowering, with correct fur volume around the carpus. Frame 7: controlled unfolding, cannon straight throughout. Frame 8: leg is about HALFWAY back down toward the original planted pose, still above the moss. Rigid bone shafts must not bow. Carpal and fetlock joints have separate anatomically correct articulation. No limb changes sides, vanishes, duplicates or becomes a thin cable. Body mostly steady, no bouncing/sliding, all antlers visible. Correct overlap of lifted limb with nearer planted foreleg. Each cell is a new well-drawn anatomical pose matching this SAME deer, not an image geometrically squeezed. Maintain even blank margins and exact fixed hoof/ground anchors. Clean transparent edges and identical gold rim light. Read cells left-to-right then next row. The complete full body and island must fit each cell.

Asset: exactly EIGHT sequential photoreal animation frames in a FOUR-column TWO-row grid, equal 2:3 portrait cells, whole sheet wide 4:3, genuine transparent background, NO borders/text/labels. This is the controlled lowering, contact and settling of the SAME approved deer. Input1 is the exact approved final resting stance and character/terrain identity. Input2 is the immediately preceding half-lowered foreleg frame; begin with that pose. Keep face, eyes, antler topology, coat spot pattern, torso shape, scale, camera, margins and moss/flower/rock island consistent across ALL cells. Three planted hooves remain at their exact original anchors. The moving limb is ONLY the farther (image-left) foreleg. It must return to its ORIGINAL planted location from input1, visibly LEFT of the nearer planted foreleg; do not merge or cross the forelegs. Frame1 starts from input2's partial lowering. Frame2: the cannon unfolds, cloven hoof descends and moves gently forward toward its original site. Frame3: further gradual downward/forward motion, separate normal carpal and fetlock articulation. Frame4: hoof approaches the moss, still just above it. Frame5: hoof first touches the original resting anchor from input1. Frame6: accept weight with tiny natural joint compression. Frame7: settle and straighten to the natural resting stance. Frame8: exactly input1's four-hoof resting stance again. Maintain straight rigid bone shafts and normal flesh volume; no thin cable-like leg, elongated hooked hoof, extra limb, disappearing far leg, double hoof, bowing cannon or impossible joint angles. Depict genuinely new anatomy drawings each frame, not warped photo copies. The upper body remains almost still; no bouncing or sliding. Complete antlers and hooves visible in each cell; consistent warm gold rim lighting and clean alpha edges. Correct contact shadow, fur overlap and grass overlap at the moving hoof. Read left-to-right top row then bottom row. The last cell must match the first input's rest pose for a clean handoff.
